profile.reading:
This building, RagingWire CA2 (now branded NTT Sacramento CA2), is the second of three buildings on NTT's Sacramento campus. NTT's own facility page publishes 87,855 square feet of data floor (technical) space, 26.1 megawatts of critical IT load, and states the building is LEED Gold certified and EPA ENERGY STAR rated, notably more environmental certification than NTT discloses for its CA1 or CA3 buildings on the same campus. A discrepancy worth flagging: NTT's own CA2 facility page lists the street address as 1200 Striker Ave., Sacramento, CA 95834, identical to the address NTT publishes for CA1, which this registry's independently geocoded property data instead places at 1312 Striker Ave., Sacramento, CA 95834; this reads as a likely address-field duplication error on NTT's own site template rather than a real shared address, so this entry keeps the independently geocoded street number rather than adopting NTT's duplicated figure as fact. Separately, NTT's Sacramento campus overview page states 266,000 square feet of total data floor space campus-wide, while CA1 (85,000 sq ft) plus CA2 (87,855 sq ft) plus CA3 (64,723 sq ft) sum to 237,578 square feet, a roughly 28,400-square-foot gap between the campus total and the sum of the three named buildings that this registry is not able to resolve from NTT's public materials and is flagging rather than papering over. The campus-wide capacity figure does reconcile: 12.6 + 26.1 + 14 megawatts sums to 52.7 megawatts, matching NTT's stated campus total.

NTT's US Global Data Centers footprint spans seven named campuses in total: Ashburn, Virginia at 224 megawatts; Chicago, Illinois at more than 200 megawatts; Dallas, Texas at 160 megawatts; Hillsboro, Oregon at 126 megawatts; Phoenix, Arizona at 240 megawatts; and a combined Sacramento/Santa Clara, California figure of 68 megawatts, totaling roughly 1,118 megawatts or more of disclosed US capacity, per the operator's own locations page. The US business operates under the NTT DATA Global Data Centers Americas name, the successor brand to RagingWire Data Centers, now under Japan's NTT DATA Group and parent Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation, a Tokyo Stock Exchange-listed company not subject to SEC 10-K filing requirements.

A previously confirmed, specific data center acquisition remains NTT Communications purchase of an 86.7 percent stake in e-shelter, described as Germany top data center operator, completed around June 23, 2015, though that acquisition is not directly connected to this United States facility. reading.body:
The operator has confirmed a 52.7 MW data center campus in Sacramento across three buildings, CA1, CA2, and CA3, with 266,000 square feet of total data floor space. The published capacity applies to the entire campus, not to CA2 specifically. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this 52.7 MW represents roughly 1,300 racks, though the actual mix of workloads and power densities is not published.

California has published capacity figures for only 11 facilities out of 103 mapped data center sites in the state, totaling 365 MW. This Sacramento campus does not rank in the top 11 by the published figures available to this site, placing it outside the state's disclosed major capacity. No per-building specifications, power distribution details, cooling architecture, grid connection capacity, or water sourcing are published.

The operator NTT is a global telecommunications and IT services company with substantial data center operations worldwide, but the Sacramento facility's design specification, customer qualification, or planned utilization is not published. The campus location adjacent to Sacramento International Airport places it within an existing industrial business park corridor, but local grid conditions, interconnection status, and available headroom for expansion are not in the published record.
